findings.title: raw_spec type hint contradicts defensive or-empty guard
findings.why_it_matters: The parameter is declared `dict[str, Any]` (never None), yet `dict(raw_spec or {})` signals to callers that None is a valid input. This is a contract contradiction: static analysers will trust the annotation and skip the None path, while the runtime guard silently accepts None. Either widen the type to `dict[str, Any] | None` or drop the `or {}` guard. The same pattern appears in `_normalize_template_registry` at the analogous `raw_registry or {}` guard.
findings.suggested_fix: If None is genuinely possible from callers, annotate both parameters as `dict[str, Any] | None` with defaults. If None is never expected, drop the `or {}` fallback and let a TypeError surface early.

findings.title: load_template_registry uses stale family key post-normalization
findings.why_it_matters: After `_normalize_template_registry` runs, every action spec is guaranteed to have `filename_prefix`. The L0 cache warm-up loop on line 1096 still reads `act.get('family', '')` instead of `act.get('filename_prefix', '')` or `act['filename_prefix']`. The compat alias `spec['family'] = filename_prefix` means the current behavior is accidentally correct, but it creates a dependency on the alias surviving. If the PLANNED Step 11 removes the compat alias this loop silently starts keying the cache on empty strings, breaking all L0 reference lookups without any error at the broken call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 1096 to `family = act.get('filename_prefix', '')` and update the same pattern at line 1113 in `_load_reference_l0`. These are the two sites that will break when the compat alias is removed.
evidence: line 1016: `spec['family'] = filename_prefix`  # compat alias comment warns it will be removed

findings.title: _normalize_template_registry mutates registry dict in-place then returns it
findings.why_it_matters: `dict(raw_registry or {})` creates a shallow copy, but then the loop body does `ts = dict(template_set or {})` and writes `registry['template_sets'] = normalized_sets` — so the top-level copy is fine. However, `prefix_catalog` and `skin_family_scope` values are not deep-copied; their nested structures are mutated in-place via direct assignment if the validation loop or caller mutates them later. The function name does not signal that it returns a partially-shared structure. In a module with a global cache (`_template_registry`) that returns the same object to all callers, this is a latent aliasing hazard.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `import copy; registry = copy.deepcopy(raw_registry)` instead of a shallow `dict(...)` copy, or document explicitly that the returned registry is not safe to mutate after assignment to the global cache.
evidence: line 1021: `registry = dict(raw_registry or {})`  # shallow copy only
line 950: `_template_registry: dict[str, Any] | None = None`  # global cache returned to all callers

findings.title: ValueError on bad registry data is unhandled at load site
findings.why_it_matters: `_normalize_template_registry` raises `ValueError` for any schema violation. `load_template_registry()` calls it with no try/except, so a malformed `template_registry.json` propagates an unhandled `ValueError` through the Flask request cycle. Flask will catch it and return a 500, but `_template_registry` will remain `None`, causing every subsequent request to retry the failing load. This is an unbounded per-request file-read-and-crash loop. The empty-file fallback path at line 1090 sets `_template_registry` before returning; the normalize path does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either catch `ValueError` in `load_template_registry()` and assign a sentinel (e.g., `{'template_sets': {}, 'schema_version': 2, '_load_error': str(e)}`) to `_template_registry` before re-raising, or document clearly in a comment that re-tries on every request are expected and acceptable.
evidence: line 1086-1099: `load_template_registry` — no try/except around normalize call
line 1023-1030: `_normalize_template_registry` raises ValueError for structural errors
line 1090: empty-file path sets `_template_registry` before returning — normalize path does not

findings.title: _resolve_preview_xp_fields not annotated with return type in prior code
findings.why_it_matters: The function `_resolve_preview_xp_fields` was introduced alongside the normalize functions; its return type `tuple[str, str]` is correctly annotated. This is fine. However, the private helper does not have a parameter annotation for `spec`: it is `spec: dict[str, Any]` which is correct. No issue here — this finding is suppressed.

findings.title: prefix_catalog drift check uses str() coercion masking type errors
findings.why_it_matters: The drift-check loop applies `str(ps.get(field) or '').strip()` to both prefix and action field values before comparing. This will silently coerce non-string values (integers, lists, None) to a string representation before comparing, meaning a field drift where one side is an integer and the other is the string form of that integer would not be caught. The intent seems to be equality of string paths, but the coercion hides schema bugs rather than raising on them.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert that both values are already `str` instances before comparing, or add a separate type-check pass in `_normalize_template_registry` that validates expected field types.

residual_risks: The compat alias `spec['family'] = filename_prefix` creates a time-bomb: two call sites (lines 1096 and 1113) read 'family' and will silently break when Step 11 removes the alias. The alias and its planned removal are noted in a comment but there is no test that would catch the regression at removal time.

_template_registry is module-level mutable state returned by reference to all callers. Any caller that mutates the returned dict (e.g., the old `reg['enabled_families'] = sorted(ENABLED_FAMILIES)` pattern in app.py, now removed) would corrupt the cache for all subsequent requests. The removal of that mutation in this diff is the right fix, but no guard prevents future similar mutations.
The normalize functions raise ValueError on schema violations that propagate as 500s with no cache sentinel, causing a repeated file-read-and-fail loop on every request until the server restarts.
testing_gaps: No test covers `_normalize_template_registry` with a malformed template_registry.json (e.g., `template_sets` not a dict, or an action missing all normalized fields). The happy-path tests in test_template_registry_schema.py are thorough but there are no negative-path unit tests for the normalize functions.

No test verifies behavior when `load_template_registry()` is called after a previous call raised ValueError mid-normalization — i.e., that `_template_registry` remains None and the next call retries (rather than returning a partial result).

The L0 cache warm-up at line 1096 is exercised only indirectly through integration tests. A unit test that directly calls `_load_reference_l0` with a known family key after normalization would confirm the family-key aliasing is working and would catch the regression when the compat alias is eventually removed.
